hypothesisOutcomes.question: Command-policy composition and precedence: org floor, allow/deny/approval, malformed rules, shell parsing/normalization and actual execution consumers.
hypothesisOutcomes.outcome: CONFIRMED_WITH_EVIDENCE. composePolicy() always prepends org-floor rules before scope rules (org evaluates first, so it structurally cannot be shadowed by a later scope carve-out) and mode composition is one-way: an org allowlist cannot be downgraded to denylist by a scope, but a scope MAY tighten an org denylist into an allowlist (test/command-policy.test.ts, 2 cases). evaluateCommandWithLayer adds a third tier (deployment-specific layer rules) that applies only when the scope policy is silent and can never override an explicit scope decision, including an allowlist's implicit deny (test/command-policy.test.ts).
